chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Idris, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abdullah ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:

I read the book of Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) in his own handwriting: 'Convey to my Shias that my visitation (Ziyarah) equals in the sight of Allah one thousand accepted Hajjs and one thousand accepted Umras in their entirety.' I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'One thousand Hajjs?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah, and one thousand thousand Hajjs for whoever visits him while being cognizant of his right.'

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation or pilgrimage to a holy figure or shrine
key_terms.عَارِفاً: One who possesses deep knowledge and recognition

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of Ziyarah (visiting the Imam) according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith emphasizes the preeminence of Ziyarat (visitation) as a means of spiritual connection, equating a single visit to Imam al-Rida with a thousand accepted Hajjs and Umras. The narration further clarifies that this reward is multiplied for those who visit with *Ma'rifah* (gnostic recognition) of the Imam's specific rights and status, highlighting the Shia emphasis on inner knowledge over mere ritual performance. This underscores the theological view that the Imam serves as the spiritual axis of the earth, making his visitation a direct conduit to divine acceptance.
